title: Cityline Transit - Implementation Kickoff & VPC Intake
next_steps: Redwood to send staging runbook and VPC peering checklist by 2027-06-20
Schedule security deep-dive with Cityline SecOps the week of 2027-06-28
Customer to provide list of sample workloads and traffic patterns by 2027-06-22
action_items: Priya - generate recommended instance / GPU sizing for 1k qps pilot - due 2027-06-21
Aisha - open firewall ticket and share VPC subnet CIDRs - due 2027-06-20
Maya - send contract summary and pilot P1 SLA targets - due 2027-06-19
summary: Kickoff for Cityline Transit onboarding. Goals: confirm success criteria for a 6-week pilot, validate VPC network needs, review security/compliance requirements (data residency, KMS), and schedule a SecOps deep-dive. Customer prefers Redwood Private in VPC first, may expand to Dedicated later.
topics: Security: encryption, KMS, audit logs, SOC2
Latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching and caching suggestions
questions: What telemetry will Redwood need for observability?
Can we support Cityline's on-prem message bus in the pilot?
How does token retention and logs work with KMS enabled?
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-06-18 14:00 UTC; Duration: ~54 minutes; Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Tom Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Jordan Miles (Head of Platform, Cityline), Aisha Rahman (DevOps), Diego Suarez (Product), Lily Park (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick round-robin please?
[00:08] Jordan: Jordan here, Head of Platform at Cityline. We're building out an LLM-assisted ops assistant for dispatch and incident summarization.
[00:15] Aisha: Aisha, I run DevOps and networking for Cityline. I'll own the VPC peering and firewall work.
[00:21] Diego: Diego, product. I'll handle acceptance criteria and evaluation.
[00:26] Maya: Great. Tom and Priya with me — Tom will manage the onboarding cadence and runbook, Priya will cover infra sizing and tests.
[00:35] Priya: Hi. Quick note: we'll propose a pilot config and then iterate. Also, we often call our VPC option Redwood Private — sometimes the docs say "Private control plane" which is the same thing.
[00:44] Jordan: Sounds good. Our timeline: 6-week pilot starting early July if we can get staging by end of next week. Critical path is the network handoff and security approvals.
[00:54] Maya: Understood. Let's align on success criteria — Diego, what does the product team need to see to call the pilot success?
[01:01] Diego: Three things: 1) 95th percentile latency under 200ms for single-turn prompts in staging, 2) semantic accuracy on our dispatch tasks above our baseline (we'll share evals), and 3) stable integration with our event bus without leaks or PII exposure.
[01:20] Priya: For latency, is that cold-start or steady-state? If you do a steady-state with batching enabled, we can hit lower per-token cost but latency numbers depend on batching window. We can tune for low-latency at cost tradeoff.
[01:36] Jordan: Prefer few-hundred ms tail latency, but Diego will give specific prompt profiles.
[01:42] Tom: I'll note that's a tradeoff: we can run a configuration that prioritizes latency for the pilot, and later tune batching/quantization for cost.
[01:50] Lily: From security: we require KMS-integration for encryption at rest, RBAC for access, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SOC2 attestation or equivalent. Do you support customer-managed KMS?
[02:05] Priya: Yes, Redwood Private in VPC supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; there's also a dedicated option for on-prem keys. For hosted API we offer server-side keys but given your compliance needs, we recommend VPC with your KMS.
[02:21] Aisha: We also need an architecture sketch — public IPs, egress patterns, and which ports Redwood needs.
[02:29] Maya: We'll send a VPC peering checklist. For peering we only need outbound egress on TCP 443 to our control plane endpoints, plus optional SSH for jump hosts if you want direct access to staging. We'll add exact CIDRs in the checklist.
[02:44] Jordan: Can you support an on-prem message bus? Our dispatch events flow on an internal Kafka cluster. We don't want to egress that data outside our VPC.
[02:55] Priya: Two approaches: 1) Proxy the events to a staging queue inside your VPC that Redwood can ingest via private peering (recommended), or 2) deploy a small adapter inside your network that calls Redwood over VPC endpoint using mutual TLS. We can help with both.
[03:16] Diego: What's the expected data retention? We can't afford full transcripts to persist longer than 30 days. Encryption and purge controls are mandatory.
[03:25] Maya: We have retention policies configurable per-customer; with Redwood Private you can enforce a 30-day retention and we can disable long-term logging of prompt/response pairs. Audit logs will still show metadata for operations.
[03:38] Lily: Do audit logs include token-level info? That's sensitive.
[03:43] Priya: By default, logs include metadata like request id, duration, model used; token content can be redacted. For forensic needs we can enable encrypted log archival to your S3 with KMS wrapping, but that requires additional SOC approval.
[04:01] Aisha: Network checklist — do you need us to open ingress or only allow egress?
[04:06] Tom: Generally egress only from your VPC to ours, we don't require inbound open ports into Cityline. For telemetry and traces, we push metrics to your configured collector over a secure connection.
[04:17] Jordan: For the pilot load, expect ~1k requests per minute during peak, mostly short prompts (~30-80 tokens). We will provide sample histograms.
[04:29] Priya: Good. For 1k RPM with low-latency target, we'll recommend a small Dedicated-like pool in staging (N gpus), but for the pilot we can run on Redwood Private with reserved capacity profiles. I'll size after we get exact QPS and token length distributions.
[04:45] Maya: We'll also propose canary rollout steps and rollback in case of quality regressions. Diego, you'll own acceptance checks?
[04:52] Diego: Yes, product will run evals against our golden prompt set. We expect Redwood to run parallel A/B tests and report drift/regressions.
[05:02] Lily: On personnel — who will be our point for security follow-ups?
[05:06] Maya: Lily, you'll get Tom for operational runbook and I'll loop in our security lead (name: Rajeev Patel) for the SecOps deep-dive.
[05:15] Tom: We should schedule that next week. Is Tuesday 2027-06-29 at 15:00 UTC workable?
[05:22] Lily: That works.
[05:24] Aisha: Are there any special network appliances or proxies Redwood needs to support? We use an in-line WAF and NAT gateways.
[05:32] Priya: No special appliances; NAT egress is fine. If you have an internal proxy, we'll provide a list of endpoints to whitelist.
[05:40] Jordan: What's the SLA for pilot? We don't need enterprise SLA but we want clear uptime and latency SLOs for the pilot.
[05:48] Maya: For pilots we usually commit to an availability baseline in the runbook and target latency envelopes; full SLA and credits are part of Dedicated/reserved terms which we can outline in the contract. I'll send a pilot SLA summary.
[05:59] Diego: Regarding model versions — would we be pinned to a specific model during pilot, or can Redwood do live rollouts?
[06:06] Priya: We can pin a model version for stability and run controlled rollouts for upgrades. There are rollback policies and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if a model degrades.
[06:16] Aisha: Any specific telemetry you need from our side to debug latency spikes?
[06:21] Tom: Request ids and timing traces are helpful; we will instrument trace headers in responses so you can correlate. We also provide token-level timing (optional, redacted) for perf tuning.
[06:33] Jordan: Competitors question — our infra team evaluated SageAI but they didn't offer VPC/KMS integration in the same way. Is that one reason customers choose Redwood?
[06:44] Maya: Yes — many customers choose Redwood for private/VPC options and stronger runbook/ops support for production inference.
[06:52] Diego: One operational ask — we want an endpoint for synthetic traffic testing and a small benchmark harness.
[06:58] Priya: We'll provide a benchmarking script and a staging endpoint; we recommend running your harness overnight to capture warm cache behavior.
[07:09] Tom: Recap of immediate blockers: VPC CIDRs from Aisha, sample traffic patterns from Diego, and a security contact from Lily to schedule deep-dive.
[07:20] Aisha: I'll share CIDRs by EOD 2027-06-20 and open the firewall ticket.
[07:27] Diego: We'll export the histogram and golden prompts by Monday 2027-06-21.
[07:32] Lily: I'll confirm SecOps availability for the 29th.
[07:36] Maya: Great. Priya — you'll follow up on sizing and staging config?
[07:41] Priya: Yes, I'll send a recommended staging config (GPU type, batch settings, cache config) and a pilot cost estimate by 2027-06-21.
[07:51] Jordan: One more question — how do you handle PII or ticket redaction if an agent sends a driver's license number?
[07:58] Priya: We can enable automatic redaction hooks and set up on-the-fly filters; plus, you can route raw logs to your S3 and keep only redacted copies in our control plane. We'll include redaction patterns in the runbook.
[08:12] Maya: Okay let's close with a clear set of next steps and owners. Tom, can you summarize?
[08:18] Tom: Sure — 1) Redwood: send VPC peering checklist, staging runbook, benchmarking harness, and pilot SLA summary (Maya/Priya) by 2027-06-20. 2) Customer: provide CIDRs and firewall ticket (Aisha) by 2027-06-20; provide traffic histograms and golden prompts (Diego) by 2027-06-21; confirm SecOps attendee (Lily) by 2027-06-22. 3) Schedule SecOps deep-dive on 2027-06-29.
[08:48] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the runbook and calendar invites.
[08:54] Jordan: Appreciate it, looking forward to the pilot.
[09:00] End of meeting.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-hearings; "KV cache" at one point transcribed as "K-V cash" in automated notes. References: runbook link (docx) will be shared in follow-up, staging endpoints will be provisioned after VPC peering is established.
